newsitem.title: MEXICO: BASEBALL-CARIBBEAN SERIES TO SHOWCASE LATIN AMERICAN TALENT.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CARIBBEAN SERIES TO SHOWCASE LATIN AMERICAN TALENT.

text.p: Baseball's Caribbean Series kicks off Tuesday with Latin American bragging rights at stake as the winter league champions from Mexico, Venezuela, Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic face off.
The desert city setting is far from the Caribbean, but thousands of fans from the three visiting nations are packing Hermosillo's hotels.
The competition is expected to be stiff, with each team bringing a share of Major League players to the fray.
With 13 major leaguers packing their lineup, Puerto Rico's Indios de Mayaguez (Mayaguez Indians) -- led by Baltimore Orioles superstar Roberto Alomar -- are hot favourites.

But last year's favourites from the Dominican Republic, a "Dream Team" of major league stars, flopped miserably as Mexico's Tomateros de Culiacan (Culiacan Tomato Growers) took the title, becoming the first Mexican team in 10 years to win the series.

Culiacan is back after winning the Mexican Pacific League. The other two teams battling for the Caribbean title are the Aguilas de Cibao (Cibao Eagles) of the Dominican Republic and the Navegantes de Magallanes (Magellan Navigators) of Venezuela.
Each team will take on the other three twice in a round-robin format set to end Sunday. The team with the best six-game record wins, with a playoff to be held in the event of a tie.
Puerto Rico opens the series Tuesday against the Dominican Republic, after which Mexico takes on Venezuela.
The Mexican team suffered a setback when star shortstop Benjamin Gil, who spends his summers with the Texas Rangers, pulled out of the series with a leg injury.
Mexican Manager Francisco Estrada said Gil injury was "a serious casualty for our team" but expressed confidence that Culiacan could repeat as champions.

"Now it can no longer be said as it was before that Mexico is the ugly step-child of the Caribbean Series because our baseball has progressed a lot and can compete head to head with the champions from Puerto Rico, Venezuela and the Dominican Republic," Estrada told the Hermosillo daily newspaper El Imparcial.
Gil's injury leaves Mexico with just one Major Leaguer in Juan Gabriel Castro of the Los Angeles Dodgers.

The Tomateros Tuesday will send pitcher Martin Hernandez, who was a perfect 5-0 in the Mexican Pacific League playoffs, to the mound against a Venezuelan team led by eight major leaguers, including Alvaro Espinoza of the New York Mets and three big-league pitchers.
Puerto Rico's roster features Alomar, who won the Puerto Rican batting title with a .347 average, and Will Cordero of the Boston Red Sox, who was second in the league with a .344 average.

Eight major league players highlight the Dominican team, including first baseman Jose Offerman of the Kansas City Royals, outfielder Luis Polonia of the New York Yankees and veteran catcher Tony Pena.
